facility_roles.quote: SBND is a 112 ton liquid argon time projection chamber (LArTPC) neutrino detector located 110 meters from the Booster Neutrino Beam (BNB) target at Fermilab.

intervals.label: commissioning and first neutrinos
intervals.quote: SBND began operation in July 2024, and started collecting stable neutrino beam data in December 2024

intervals.label: stable neutrino data taking
intervals.quote: the first neutrinos have been observed by the Short-Baseline Near Detector collaboration

physics_goals.quote: SBND will measure the neutrinos as they were produced in the Fermilab beam and ICARUS will measure the neutrinos after they've potentially oscillated.
physics_goals.value: Measure the un-oscillated neutrino flux and neutrino-argon interaction rate close to the BNB target, as the near-detector reference for the SBN sterile-neutrino search

physics_goals.quote: Together SBND and ICARUS will have outstanding ability to test the existence of these new neutrinos.
physics_goals.value: Test, together with ICARUS, the existence of a sterile neutrino

physics_goals.quote: We will collect 10 times more data on how neutrinos interact with argon than all previous experiments combined
physics_goals.value: Collect a large sample of neutrino-argon interactions to support future liquid-argon experiments such as DUNE

summary.plain: The newest and closest of Fermilab's three short-baseline liquid-argon detectors, sitting right next to where the neutrino beam is made so it can measure the beam before anything has a chance to change.
summary.technical: Near detector of the Short-Baseline Neutrino programme: 112 t active-mass single-phase LArTPC, 110 m from the BNB target at Fermilab. Began operation July 2024; stable neutrino data taking (~7,000 events/day) from December 2024/first-neutrinos announcement 10 September 2024.

unique_capabilities.quote: SBND began operation in July 2024, and started collecting stable neutrino beam data in December 2024 with an unprecedented rate of ~7,000 neutrino events per day.
unique_capabilities.value: Closest of the three SBN detectors to the beam target, seeing an unprecedented ~7,000 neutrino events per day
